notes.account: The author begins with Posons and defines Sigma_12, E_1, and E_2 in (13). The written first subscript in the E_2 intersection is 1. The source diagram places E_2 below Sigma_2^+ and Sigma_12. This discrepancy was noticed as a source comparison; the definition was not changed to match the diagram.

The author calls (14) a diagram of inclusions of closed parts of X, then describes the three squares as cartésiens et cocartésiens. Ten ordinary arrows point toward the next higher row. A further lower arrow toward E_1 is scratched. The bottom glyph remains uncertain. H's statement that cartésiens stands above and after cocartésiens does not describe its visible baseline position on this scan.

The marginal NB records the empty intersection of the two positive Sigma terms, two further empty intersections, two inclusions into Sigma terms carrying a high ring and minus, and a final E_1/E_2 intersection. The written second intersection has Sigma_1^-; the ring identity and extra low stroke before the last equality remain uncertain.

The author gives the unnumbered square equations and the two further pairs labelled (15). In (15), the right-hand first-row Sigma has two 2-shaped digits, and the relation below the small written (13) has three separate bars. These ink readings have been retained despite the parallel occurrences of 12 and equality. Older indices and high signs are partially overdrawn.

The source lists three nonempty intersections in (16), then refers to the last relation and calls the first two “les deux premières étant évidentes”. An added word read first as Prouvons introduces that discussion. This is the author's own claim and wording; no proof check is claimed by this reader.

The final paragraph records the author's argument beginning “Si on ...”. It uses the displayed inclusion of E_1 and E_2 in Sigma_12, refers to Pi_1 and Pi_2 as two underlined “partitions” of X “en des parties non vides”, and ends with the two live complement formulas. The abandoned inline and display expressions remain in the transcription, including their uncertain letters and signs. The later live formulas did not supply missing glyphs in the abandoned inline expression.
